title: Strings
test_conventions: Tests are Python assert snippets executed AFTER the learner's code, in the same namespace, one snippet at a time. Everything the learner's code printed is available to tests as the string variable __stdout__, and the learner's source code is available as the string __source__ (some hidden tests re-run that source with different input values to make sure the result is computed, not typed). expected_output comparisons are exact after stripping trailing whitespace on each line (and trailing blank lines). tests[].visible defaults to true; visible:false tests are hidden and always carry a failure_message. For fill_blank, blanks in starter_code are written ___ and are filled in order; every alternative in blanks[].answer must pass the tests. For parsons, lines are shown shuffled; correct_order lists, for each position of the solution, the index into lines; distractors are extra lines that must not be used. For predict, expected_output must be one of choices; for debug with expected_output the fixed program's stdout must match it exactly.

worked_example.code:
first_name, last_name = 'Elif', 'Yılmaz'
full_name = first_name + ' ' + last_name
print(full_name, len(full_name))
print('-' * 12)
print('Ad\tYaş\nElif\t21')
notes: + glues strings with nothing in between, so the space must be added as its own string.
* repeats a string, which gives a quick separator line of any length.
\t and \n are single characters inside the string: a tab and a line break, so one print produces two aligned lines.
notes_tr: + metinleri aralarına hiçbir şey koymadan yapıştırır; bu yüzden boşluk ayrı bir string olarak eklenmelidir.
* bir string'i tekrarlar; bu, istediğin uzunlukta hızlı bir ayraç çizgisi verir.
\t ve \n string içinde tek birer karakterdir: sekme ve satır sonu; bu yüzden tek bir print iki hizalı satır üretir.

blocks.concept_tr: f-string ve biçim belirteçleri (% ve format ile birlikte)

worked_example.code:
name, count, total = 'Elif', 3, 149.7
print(f'{name}: {count} ürün, {total:.2f} TL')
rate = 0.256
print(f'İndirim oranı: {rate:.1%}')
print(f'{"Kahve":<8}{45:>6.2f}')
notes: An f-string evaluates every expression in braces and inserts the result, so no str() is needed.
After a colon comes a format specifier: .2f means two decimal places and .1% shows a fraction as a percentage with one decimal.
<8 and >6 set a field width and alignment, which keeps the columns of a receipt in line.
notes_tr: Bir f-string süslü parantezdeki her ifadeyi hesaplar ve sonucu yerleştirir; bu yüzden str() gerekmez.
İki noktadan sonra biçim belirteci gelir: .2f iki ondalık basamak demektir, .1% bir kesri tek ondalıklı yüzde olarak gösterir.
<8 ve >6 alan genişliğini ve hizalamayı belirler; bu, bir fişin sütunlarını hizalı tutar.

blocks.concept_tr: Metin temizleme: strip, replace, split, join ve büyük-küçük harf

worked_example.code:
raw = '  Facebook, Google, Microsoft  '
clean = raw.strip()
companies = clean.split(', ')
print(companies, len(companies))
print(' # '.join(companies))
print(clean.replace('Google', 'Alphabet').upper())
notes: strip() removes the spaces at both ends, which is almost always the first step for input from outside.
split(', ') cuts at every comma followed by a space and returns a list; join() is the opposite and is called on the separator.
replace() and upper() each return a new string, so they can be chained from left to right.
notes_tr: strip() iki uçtaki boşlukları siler; dışarıdan gelen girdi için neredeyse her zaman ilk adımdır.
split(', ') her virgül-boşluk ikilisinde keser ve bir liste döndürür; join() bunun tersidir ve ayırıcı üzerinde çağrılır.
replace() ve upper() her biri yeni bir string döndürür; bu yüzden soldan sağa zincirlenebilir.

exercises.model_answer: join() is a method of the separator string: the separator is the object that knows how to glue, and it takes the list of strings as its argument. split() is the opposite: it is called on a text and returns a list of the pieces between the separators.
exercises.model_answer_tr: join() ayırıcı string'in bir metodudur: yapıştırmayı bilen nesne ayırıcıdır ve string listesini argüman olarak alır. split() bunun tersidir: bir metin üzerinde çağrılır ve ayırıcıların arasındaki parçalardan oluşan bir liste döndürür.
